findings.title: An AGL quota left open by one party of a shared transaction makes the next AGL trade in that transaction revert
findings.difference: No chain rule is involved beyond the fact that carriers such as ERC-4337 bundles put the calls of several users into one transaction with one transient storage map. AGL 0x0000000000109de411eabc9f04906d79f06fda0e and its hook PoolAGL 0x0000000456b76bc801253ef2366664750f602840 hold code on OP Mainnet and Base (15,125 and 8,730 bytes), and cota() reads 0 outside a transaction.
findings.mechanism: PoolAGL keeps one signed quota in a transient slot. afterSwap adds the negated AGL amount of the swapper to it. The token calls consumirSaida when AGL leaves the PoolManager, which needs a quota that is zero or negative and at least as large as the amount, and consumirEntrada when AGL enters, which needs a quota that is zero or positive and at least as large as the amount. Nothing resets the quota when an unlock ends. Step 1: party A buys X AGL in the official pool, which sets the quota to minus X, and closes its unlock with mint in place of take. mint moves no token (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329), so the quota stays at minus X. Step 2: party B, later in the same transaction, sells Y AGL. Its swap moves the quota to Y minus X. Its payment of Y AGL into the PoolManager calls consumirEntrada, which reverts with ForaDaCota because the quota is below Y, so the transfer and the unlock of B revert. The mirror case holds for a seller A who pays with burned claims and a buyer B whose take then fails in consumirSaida. Step 3: a party B that holds AGL claims can burn them and take up to X AGL against the quota that A left, without a swap of its own, which is the only case where a claim on AGL turns into tokens outside a swap. I read the hook source and did not simulate the two party sequence on chain. The token side of the calls is taken from the reading recorded under F-074 in cycle 4.
findings.impact: A later user of a shared transaction who trades AGL has its operation reverted and pays its gas. No balance moves to the party that left the quota, which paid the 2 percent pool fee on its own swap. Nothing outside the AGL pool is affected.
findings.preconditions: Two parties trade AGL inside one transaction, for example two user operations of one bundle, and the first one settles its AGL side with ERC-6909 claims. The first party must hold or accept AGL claims.
findings.mitigations: Routers that trade AGL can read cota() before the swap and refuse to proceed when it is not zero. Bundlers can keep AGL operations of different senders in separate transactions. Core cannot change the behaviour of a token hook.

sources.supports: Verified source of PoolAGL: the transient quota, afterSwap adding the negated AGL delta, consumirEntrada and consumirSaida with their sign checks, and no reset of the quota.
eth_getCode of the token and the hook (15,125 and 8,730 bytes) and cota() returning 0 on OP Mainnet; the same reads on https://mainnet.base.org/ for Base.

verification.factCheck: eth_getCode on https://mainnet.optimism.io (block 159,929,911) and https://mainnet.base.org/ (block 61,341,130) returned 15,125 bytes for AGL 0x0000000000109de411eabc9f04906d79f06fda0e and 8,730 bytes for PoolAGL 0x0000000456b76bc801253ef2366664750f602840 on both chains. On both chains cota() returns 0, lancado() returns true, token() returns the AGL address and poolManager() returns the PoolManager of state/networks.json. The verified PoolAGL source was fetched from Celo Blockscout and from explorer.optimism.io and the two texts are identical (sha256 prefix 0d637f057cabfcdc). It keeps one signed quota in transient slot SLOT_ENTRADA (line 66). afterSwap adds the negated AGL amount of the swap delta (lines 203 to 211). consumirEntrada reverts with ForaDaCota unless the quota is at least zero and at least the amount (lines 218 to 223). consumirSaida reverts unless the quota is at most zero and its magnitude is at least the amount (lines 228 to 233). The quota is written only at lines 209, 222, 232, 348 and 377, and no line resets it when an unlock ends. The low 14 bits of the hook address are 0x2840, which are the beforeInitialize, beforeAddLiquidity and afterSwap flags. The verified AGL source (same two explorers, identical text, sha256 prefix 16f8e61d6667272d) calls consumirEntrada in _update when the recipient is the PoolManager and consumirSaida when the sender is the PoolManager (lines 130 to 145). I tested the token side on chain, which the finding had taken from cycle 4: an eth_call of AGL.transfer(other, 1) with from set to the PoolManager reverts with 0x7c467237, ForaDaCota(1, 0), on both chains, a transfer of 1 unit into the PoolManager from another account reverts with the same error, and a transfer of 0 from the PoolManager returns true. The sequence with two parties in one transaction was not simulated, because that needs a purpose built caller contract. I did not look for a bundle or batch executor that has carried AGL trades of two parties.
verification.codeCheck: mint debits the caller's delta and writes the claim balance without any call to the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:322-329, src/ERC6909.sol:79-83), and burn is the same in reverse (src/PoolManager.sol:332-336). take calls currency.transfer with the PoolManager as msg.sender (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297, src/types/Currency.sol:60-75), which is the call the token gates, and a revert there reverts the take (src/types/Currency.sol:82-86). The hook receives the caller's swap delta in afterSwap (src/PoolManager.sol:221, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:298-303). The hook address has no return delta flag, so the returned amount is ignored (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:163). unlock checks only the PoolManager's own delta count before it locks (src/PoolManager.sol:112-113), so a first party that buys AGL and closes with mint leaves its unlock cleanly while the hook's quota stays negative. A later seller's swap in the same transaction moves the quota to its amount minus the leftover, and its payment transfer into the PoolManager then reverts inside the token before settle is reached (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). No guard in src/ changes this, because the revert happens in the token. No delta or claim of the second party is credited to the first party at any step, so no funds move between them.
verification.corrections: actor: unprivileged. The party that leaves the quota open is any account that trades in the AGL pool, and the author of the hook and token takes no step. The victims use a pool whose hook and token the attacker did not write, which is the definition of unprivileged in SCHEMA.md, and F-071 records the same shape (state left by an earlier party of a shared transaction) with that actor. The preconditions overstate the cost: the first party does not need to hold or accept claims, because clear (src/PoolManager.sol:310-319) forfeits a dust output and leaves the quota open in the same way, so one unit of AGL plus gas is enough. Effect degrade and severity low stand. The later trade reverts, can be repeated in another transaction, and no balance changes hands. The finding is not specific to OP Mainnet or Base and follows from no rule of those chains. The attacker must also get its call placed before the victim's call in one transaction, for example as the sender of an ERC-4337 bundle that contains the victim's operation. I did not confirm that any such carrier has handled an AGL trade.

findings.title: Any account can call claimFor on the MortgageFi vault share mf-e-usdc-cbbtc for the PoolManager on Base, which adds 2.58 shares to the pooled balance that the caller can book through sync and settle
findings.difference: mf-e-usdc-cbbtc 0xe443cadb4a4fa403caee0e0546c33baff32c51f8 (name mortgagefi-earn-usdc-cbbtc, 6 decimals) is a vault share on Base that pays accrued yield as new shares. Its function claimFor(address), selector 0xddeae033, pays the yield of any holder, and the caller does not have to be that holder. The cause is the token. Base adds no network property.
findings.mechanism: 1. sync stores balanceOf(PoolManager) for a currency and needs no permission (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle credits the caller with the rise of that balance since the sync (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). 2. An eth_call from the unrelated addresses 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000a11ce and 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000b0b01, through a forwarding stub placed at the caller by state override, ran claimFor(PoolManager) at Base blocks 61,347,858 and 61,347,864 on two endpoints. balanceOf(PoolManager) went from 98.714225 to 101.294415 shares, a rise of 2.580190. claimFor for an address without shares leaves the PoolManager balance unchanged. 3. A caller that runs sync(token), claimFor(PoolManager) and settle inside one unlock is credited 2.580190 shares and can take them. I did not run that sequence against the deployed PoolManager, the statement follows from the two source ranges. 4. The yield keeps accruing on the pooled shares, so the step can be repeated later. 5. The same call pattern was run for 5,477 pooled currencies on 17 networks that have a function whose name says it acts for a holder passed as argument, and for every selector of 7,835 priced currencies. This token and the known ibBUSD (F-090) are the only ones where the PoolManager balance of a currency with a market changes. The token uniusd.fun 0xd98a61961ca8a8a53eaf48f2d6d5af5fe134c801 on Base also raises it, through collectTo(address), but that function mints 875 units to any address for any caller, so the token has no backing to lose.
findings.impact: 2.58 shares, about 2.64 USD at the GeckoTerminal price of 1.0214 USD per share, out of 98.71 shares (about 100.83 USD) that the PoolManager holds for the hookless pool 0x620bc43c2198b61932b13aabbfdba4f6e0b236d6dca7282711277856175b0895 (USDC and mf-e-usdc-cbbtc, fee 0.01 percent, tick spacing 1, no hook; the pool id equals the hash of these five values). The yield belongs to the liquidity providers of that pool in economic terms. They cannot claim it, and any account can.
findings.preconditions: Accrued yield on the shares held by the PoolManager. It is 2.58 shares today.
findings.mitigations: Liquidity providers should not hold yield paying vault shares in a pool when the yield can be claimed for a holder by anyone. Interfaces can flag receipt tokens that have claimFor(address).

verification.factCheck: I ran one eth_simulateV1 request without state overrides on mainnet.base.org and on base-rpc.publicnode.com at block 61,361,038, with the same result on both. balanceOf(PoolManager) on 0xe443cadb4a4fa403caee0e0546c33baff32c51f8 is 98,714,225 base units and totalSupply is 10,721,408,987. claimFor(PoolManager), selector 0xddeae033, sent by the unrelated account 0x00000000000000000000000000000000000a11ce, succeeds and logs Transfer(zero address, PoolManager, 2,580,190). The balance is then 101,294,415 and totalSupply 10,723,989,177. The caller holds 0 shares before and after. A second claimFor(PoolManager) mints 0, and claimFor for an address without shares leaves the PoolManager balance unchanged. A transfer of the full 101,294,415 units from the PoolManager then passes, so the new shares are transferable. The same call also moves 90.585 USDC from the token contract to 0x87d2e27147a640092e06c9329bf8110ca9927446, which is the daily forwarding in the giveYield modifier and does not touch the PoolManager. Sourcify lists the contract as an exact match. In the source claimFor(address receiver) is public with the modifiers giveYield and fetch(receiver) and no check of the caller, and it mints claimable[receiver] to receiver (lines 167-172). transfer runs fetch for sender and recipient (line 480), so every take of the token also moves the accrued yield of the PoolManager into claimable. Owing(PoolManager) reads 2,565,472 and yieldOverwrite(PoolManager) reads the zero address. The pool id 0x620bc43c2198b61932b13aabbfdba4f6e0b236d6dca7282711277856175b0895 equals keccak256 of (USDC 0x833589fcd6edb6e08f4c7c32d4f71b54bda02913, the share token, 100, 1, zero hook), and StateView on Base returns liquidity 1,924,522,056 for it. GeckoTerminal lists this pool as the only one of the token with a price of 1.0214 USD per share.
verification.codeCheck: sync has no lock check and no caller check and stores balanceOfSelf for the currency (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288, src/types/Currency.sol:90-96). _settle reads the balance again, credits the difference to the recipient and resets the synced currency (src/PoolManager.sol:349-365). Inside one unlock a caller can call sync for the share token, call claimFor(PoolManager) on the token, call settle with no value and take the credited 2,580,190 units (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The delta is zero and unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). The msg.value check at line 356 does not apply, and the synced check of collectProtocolFees (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-52) is not on the path. Nothing ties the rise of the balance to a payment by the caller. I did not run the sequence through the deployed PoolManager, because that needs a contract.
verification.corrections: The facts and the actor stand. Three additions. 1. This is the hazard of F-081 (TITHE claimFor on Robinhood Chain) and F-041 on a second token, and it should be filed as an extension of F-081 at the same severity. 2. The liquidity providers lose no principal. The 98.71 shares stay in place, and the yield could not reach them through the PoolManager in any case, since the PoolManager cannot call claim. The loss is the accrued yield, 2.58 shares today, about 2.64 USD. 3. The token admin can redirect the yield of any holder with setOverwrite(who, receiver) (source line 179, ADMIN_ROLE). If the admin sets an overwrite for the PoolManager address, claimFor mints nothing to it and the step stops working. That part has actor issuer.

findings.title: A run of dust positions bounds how far one swap can move the price inside the transaction gas cap, and building it costs a fraction of one BNB or a few POL
findings.difference: BNB Smart Chain caps one transaction at 16,777,216 gas and Polygon at 33,554,432 gas, and Polygon charges 5460 gas for a cold storage read after PIP-88. The Avalanche C-Chain has no transaction cap below its block limit of 80,000,000 gas and charges at least half of the gas limit. Gas is cheap on all three: eth_gasPrice returned 0.05 gwei on BNB Smart Chain, 278 gwei of POL on Polygon and 7.5 gwei of AVAX on Avalanche on 2026-11-23. Ethereum has the same cap as BNB Smart Chain, and the cost of the attack in native units is what differs.
findings.mechanism: 1. Pool.swap runs one loop step for each initialized tick it reaches (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437). A step that ends on an initialized tick calls crossTick, which reads the liquidity word of the tick and reads and writes both fee growth words (src/libraries/Pool.sol:417-421 and 602-611). 2. Under Ethereum gas prices, which the BNB Smart Chain client keeps (cold read 2100, write of a non-zero slot 5000 including the cold read, fresh slot 20,000), that is three cold reads and two writes of non-zero slots, about 12,100 gas, plus the price and step arithmetic, about 16,500 gas in total. The first crossing of a tick whose fee growth words are still zero writes two fresh slots and costs about 51,000 gas. Under the Polygon prices the two figures are about 25,000 and 61,000. These figures are computed from the opcode prices in the client source and from the statements of the loop. They were not measured on chain, and the gas table of the C-Chain was not read in this cycle and is assumed equal to the Ethereum one for these opcodes. 3. One transaction can therefore cross about 1,000 already crossed ticks on BNB Smart Chain (330 on a first crossing), about 1,340 on Polygon (550) and about 4,800 on Avalanche (1,560). 4. Any account can initialize ticks. In a pool with tick spacing 1 it adds positions of one liquidity unit over consecutive ticks through modifyLiquidity (src/PoolManager.sol:145-184, src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236). Each new tick costs the account about 70,000 gas (one position slot, one tick slot, one bitmap update) and a token amount of a few base units. 1,000 ticks cost about 70 million gas, which is 0.0035 BNB, about 19.5 POL or about 0.53 AVAX at the gas prices above. With tick spacing 1, 1,000 ticks span a price change of 10.5 percent. 5. A swap that has to move the price across more initialized ticks than the cap allows runs out of gas in every transaction. The caller can still swap in pieces, because the loop stops at sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344 and 364) and each piece is a valid swap. A contract that needs the whole move in one call, such as a liquidation or a multi hop route with a fixed output, fails until it splits the swap. 6. The same bound applies without any attacker to a pool whose price sits far from its liquidity. An empty stretch costs one cold bitmap read and one step per word of 256 tick spacings (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-119). From MIN_TICK to tick 0 a pool with spacing 1 has 3,466 words, about 17 million gas at 5,000 gas per word, which is above the BNB Smart Chain cap. Finding F-102 records that any account can move the price of an empty pool for free. 7. Liquidity removal is not affected. Pool.modifyLiquidity updates two ticks, at most two bitmap words and one position and contains no loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236), so its gas does not depend on how many ticks exist.
findings.impact: No funds are taken and no withdrawal is blocked. Swaps through the affected price range of one pool need several transactions, and integrations that swap in one call across the range revert. The cost to the attacker is a one time payment of gas. The cost to swappers repeats for each traversal. The largest Quoter simulation that cycle 5 ran on BNB Smart Chain used 11,518,424 gas, so real pools already come within a factor of 1.5 of the cap without any attack.
findings.preconditions: A pool with a small tick spacing. Spacing 1 is the worst case because 1,000 ticks cover only 10.5 percent of price. The attacker needs gas and a few base units of both currencies. The price must have to cross the range, so the attack matters in volatile pairs and has no effect while the price stays on one side.
findings.mitigations: Routers and liquidators should bound each swap with sqrtPriceLimitX96 and continue in a second transaction when the limit is reached. Pool creators who expect large price moves should choose a wider tick spacing, which raises the price range that a given number of ticks covers. Interfaces can read the tick bitmap through extsload to count initialized ticks on a route before sending a swap.

verification.factCheck: I fetched the cited client sources. bnb-chain/bsc v1.8.2 params/protocol_params.go line 31 sets MaxTxGas to 1 << 24 and keeps ColdSloadCostEIP2929 2100 (line 72) and SstoreResetGasEIP2200 5000 (line 68). 0xPolygon/bor v2.11.1 params/protocol_params.go line 32 sets MaxTxGas to 1 << 25, and lines 76 and 77 set ColdSloadCostPIP88 5460 and ColdSstoreCostPIP88 2940. core/vm/operations_acl.go line 152 charges SstoreResetGasEIP2200 minus ColdSstoreCostPIP88 for a write to an existing slot. ava-labs/avalanchego v1.15.3 vms/saevm/worstcase/state.go refuses an operation only when its gas exceeds what is left of the block (Apply, lines 295 to 297) and sets the block limit from the gas rate (lines 123 and 146 to 153). On chain on 2026-11-24: eth_estimateGas of an endless loop (0x5b600056) returned gas required exceeds allowance (16777216) on bsc-dataseed1 (web3_clientVersion Geth/v1.8.2), (33554432) on polygon.drpc.org, and (50000000) on api.avax.network (avalanchego/1.15.3). The Avalanche figure is the RPC allowance of the endpoint, not a consensus cap, which fits the finding. eth_gasPrice returned 0x2faf080 (0.05 gwei), 0x4133f72d7f (about 280 gwei) and 0x1c2a6a802 (about 7.56 gwei). An eth_call that runs CLZ returned 0xff on BSC and Polygon and invalid opcode 0x1e on Avalanche. eth_call did not enforce the 2^24 cap at gas 0x4000000 on BSC, so the cap applies to transactions and estimateGas, not to eth_call. The per crossing gas figures are computed and not measured, as the finding says; the repository snapshots hold no tick crossing figure.
verification.codeCheck: The swap loop runs one step per initialized tick or per bitmap word (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344, nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord at src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-119). A step that lands on an initialized tick calls crossTick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:420), which reads and writes feeGrowthOutside0X128 and feeGrowthOutside1X128 and reads liquidityNet (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-611): three cold reads and two writes, 12,100 gas under Ethereum prices, which matches the finding. The loop ends at sqrtPriceLimitX96 (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344), so a swap can be split into valid pieces. modifyLiquidity has no loop and updates two ticks, at most two bitmap words and one position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236), so removal gas does not depend on the number of ticks. 1.0001^1000 is 1.105 and MIN_TICK/256 is 3,466 words, both as stated.
verification.corrections: The hazard is the same on Ethereum, which has the same 2^24 cap; only the native cost of building the tick run differs, so the network difference is one of price, not of rule. The Avalanche claim that the C-Chain charges at least half of the gas limit is not supported by the lines cited and was not checked. Whether the saevm code path is the one live on C-Chain mainnet was not confirmed; the client version on the endpoint is avalanchego 1.15.3.

findings.title: The sNVB rebase on the PoolManager balance was paid out to one contract in 469 transactions on BNB Smart Chain, which the earlier log source had not shown
findings.difference: No chain rule is involved. sNVB (0x6d6c16a3cbd318f3000e33cfd27662cf00f7e7c1) is the staked token of an Olympus fork. Every balance grows when the staking contract 0x6bcd1273eba684ff62614e41eff87123113112d1 runs a rebase, and finding F-066 records that any account can start the rebase once an epoch has ended. The PoolManager has held sNVB since block 49,283,730. Cycle 6 could not scan the history of this token, and the public log endpoint used then returns empty lists for old ranges.
findings.mechanism: 1. The caller opens an unlock and calls sync(sNVB), which stores balanceOf(PoolManager) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). 2. It triggers the rebase. The index rises and balanceOf(PoolManager) rises with it, with no transfer. 3. It calls settle, which credits the rise since sync to the caller (src/PoolManager.sol:358-360). 4. It calls take for the same amount, which sends the tokens out (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297), and the unlock closes with all deltas at zero (src/PoolManager.sol:112). 5. The chain shows this sequence 469 times. Each of these transactions holds a LogRebase of sNVB and a transfer of sNVB from the PoolManager, and none holds a transfer to it. 468 pay the contract 0x3c69c0620ca6bd0df44c0aa8c39602f7c3ebdf27 and one pays 0xfed56cd174406e0b2ffce9c7b1ee5113e883cdab. Twelve receipts were sampled. All twelve were sent by 0x2d68a551e7c8ecf7312ee083a16e736dce2347d5 to that contract and contain no event of the PoolManager, which fits a sequence of sync, settle and take, since none of the three emits one. 6. Archive state confirms the amounts. At block 106,450,859 the index rose from 46,185,701,171 to 46,190,184,993 and the PoolManager balance stayed at 1,407,067,071,029 base units. Without an outflow it would have been 1,407,203,672,577. The difference of 136,601,548 matches the logged transfer of 136,601,545. The same holds at blocks 108,735,661 (345,465,382 against 345,465,315) and 111,270,063 (277,199,579 against 277,199,575).
findings.impact: 94.0989 sNVB left the PoolManager, between 0.127 and 0.396 sNVB per transaction. DexScreener lists no pair for the token, so no value in USD can be given, and it is likely small. The positions in sNVB pools record fixed token amounts and do not grow with a rebase (finding F-070), so the amounts paid out were backing no position. Pool reserves stay covered. The payouts stopped at block 111,270,063. The index has grown by about 0.5 percent since then, and epoch 9,503 has been due since block 135,135,655 without anyone starting it.
findings.preconditions: The PoolManager holds the rebasing token, an epoch has ended, and the rebase can be started by any account. No role is needed. The caller pays gas only.
findings.mitigations: Core cannot tell a rebase from a payment (assumption A2). Liquidity providers should pool the wrapped form of a rebasing token, whose balance does not move. Interfaces can warn when a currency reports a balance change without a transfer. The same advice stands in F-066 and F-091.

verification.codeCheck: sync stores balanceOf(PoolManager) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). _settle credits reservesNow minus reservesBefore for the synced currency with msg.value zero (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). take debits the caller and transfers (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). The deltas close to zero, so the check at src/PoolManager.sol:112 passes. The rise from a public rebase between sync and settle is credited to the caller, which is the traced sequence.
verification.corrections: The amounts are not unpriced: the traced payout sold 136,601,545 base units of sNVB for 0.12501 BSC-USD in the same transaction through pair 0x2df8dd88da7fae1fbc995cdcd43517544b245fb3, so the total is of the order of 100 USD. findings.title: A run of dust positions bounds how far one swap can move the price inside the gas cap, and the Quoter now measures the cost per crossing on all three chains
findings.difference: BNB Smart Chain caps a transaction at 16,777,216 gas and Polygon at 33,554,432 gas. The C-Chain has no transaction cap below its block limit of 80,000,000 gas. Measured through the deployed Quoter on 2026-11-24, one initialized tick crossing in Pool.swap costs about 17,000 gas on BNB Smart Chain, about 27,700 on Polygon and 27,000 to 33,000 on the C-Chain, and one step over an empty bitmap word about 5,600, 9,200 and 4,900 to 6,400 gas.
findings.mechanism: 1. Pool.swap runs one loop step per initialized tick and per bitmap word it reaches (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344-437). A step that ends on an initialized tick calls crossTick, which reads the liquidity word and rewrites both fee growth words of the tick (src/libraries/Pool.sol:602-611). A step over an empty word reads one bitmap slot (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-121). 2. This cycle replayed the loop step by step against live storage read through extsload and called quoteExactInputSingle on the deployed Quoter at the same block, for about 60 exact input amounts per pool and direction. Every quote whose state the endpoint served returned the replay's output to the unit, so the counts of crossings and empty steps per quote are exact. 3. Pool 0x628ea54a6450645d2bb7b2911c8c6f3d7f3944c2f4703c259a1b85bf5569870b (fee 2, tick spacing 1, no hook) at block 135446931: 58 Quoter calls whose output equalled the step by step replay of Pool.swap to the unit, up to 22 initialized crossings and 246 other steps in one quote. The least squares fit gives 17,020 gas per initialized crossing and 5,577 gas per step that ends on an uninitialized word boundary, with a fixed part of 41,981 gas. At 16,777,216 gas (the BNB Smart Chain transaction cap) that is about 983 crossings or about 3,000 empty words in one transaction. 4. Pool 0xa37d3e6da98dfeb7dc8103a6614f586916a6e04d41ea0a929bc19a029de1a399 (fee 8, tick spacing 1, no hook) at block 97873763: 50 Quoter calls whose output equalled the step by step replay of Pool.swap to the unit, up to 14 initialized crossings and 493 other steps in one quote. The least squares fit gives 27,683 gas per initialized crossing and 9,174 gas per step that ends on an uninitialized word boundary, with a fixed part of 54,400 gas. At 33,554,432 gas (the Polygon transaction cap) that is about 1,210 crossings or about 3,651 empty words in one transaction. 5. Pool 0x6874d3d2b99e6b75ed2fae390907e1d921d4b06b7f48fc6d3fe9c547507e369c (fee 500, tick spacing 10, no hook) at block 101248950: 118 Quoter calls whose output equalled the step by step replay of Pool.swap to the unit, up to 155 initialized crossings and 249 other steps in one quote. The least squares fit gives 27,063 gas per initialized crossing and 6,366 gas per step that ends on an uninitialized word boundary, with a constant term of -31,275 gas, so the linear fit is only approximate for small quotes. At 80,000,000 gas (the C-Chain block gas limit, which is the only bound) that is about 2,956 crossings or about 12,566 empty words in one transaction. 6. Cycle 8 computed 16,500 gas per crossing for BNB Smart Chain and Avalanche and 25,000 for Polygon. The measurement confirms BNB Smart Chain and Polygon and shows that the C-Chain costs more than its Ethereum price assumption, so the bound there is about 2,400 to 2,950 crossings per block, not 4,800. 7. As before, any account can add one unit of liquidity on consecutive ticks of a pool with tick spacing 1 to lengthen the walk, a swapper can still cross the range in several transactions with sqrtPriceLimitX96, and liquidity removal touches two ticks without a loop (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-236).
findings.impact: No funds are taken and no withdrawal is blocked. Swaps that must cross more initialized ticks than the cap allows need several transactions, and single call integrations across that range revert. The largest single quote measured this cycle used 1,788,771 gas on BNB Smart Chain, 4,964,889 on Polygon and 5,737,630 on Avalanche.
findings.preconditions: A pool with small tick spacing and a price move that must cross the range. The attacker pays gas and a few base units of both currencies per tick.
findings.mitigations: Routers and liquidators should bound each swap with sqrtPriceLimitX96 and continue in another transaction. Interfaces can count initialized ticks on a route through extsload. On Avalanche the per crossing figure of this cycle should replace the computed one in any gas budget.

verification.codeCheck: src/libraries/Pool.sol:344 loops until amountSpecifiedRemaining is zero or the price limit is reached, and each iteration calls TickBitmap.nextInitializedTickWithinOneWord (src/libraries/TickBitmap.sol:85-121), which searches one 256 bit word and returns an uninitialized boundary when the word is empty. Pool.sol:415-428 calls crossTick only when the step reached an initialized tick, and crossTick (Pool.sol:602-611) rewrites feeGrowthOutside0X128 and feeGrowthOutside1X128 and reads liquidityNet. modifyLiquidity (Pool.sol:145-236) updates two ticks with no loop, so removal of liquidity and take of claims do not depend on the walk length. Polygon has a higher cap and a higher cost per crossing; Avalanche has no lower cap. The hazard is generic to the swap loop rather than a network difference.

findings.title: From Tempo T15 a take to a zone deposit address is forwarded to a zone portal, and a failed deposit returns to the PoolManager, where an account with callbacks in the same portal batch can book it as its own payment
findings.difference: From T15, which v1.19.1 already contains and which Tempo targets for 15 December 2026, the TIP-20 precompile treats any recipient whose bytes 4 to 12 are 0xFC as a zone virtual deposit address. A transfer to it credits the zone's portal instead of the named address and then calls depositVirtual on the portal with the sender as originator. If the zone cannot deliver the deposit, the portal refunds the originator on Tempo later, minus a fee, or parks the refund for the originator to claim.
findings.mechanism: An ordinary caller inside unlock calls take(token, to, amount) with a zone deposit address as to. The PoolManager debits the caller amount of the token (PoolManager.sol:291-297) and calls token.transfer(to, amount) (Currency.sol:53-80). The token debits the PoolManager amount, credits the portal amount, and calls the portal, whose code is a fixed system runtime that does not call the PoolManager. The call returns true, so the take succeeds, and the caller must settle amount as with any other take. The PoolManager loses exactly what the caller owes. If the deposit fails in the zone (unregistered master id, unconfigured key, rejected by the sequencer or the issuer policy), the portal later transfers the net amount to the PoolManager in a separate transaction, or parks it under the PoolManager's address, which the PoolManager can never claim because it makes no arbitrary calls. A refund that arrives with no sync before it raises balanceOf(PoolManager) and credits no caller (PoolManager.sol:279-288, 349-364), so it stays as surplus. A reading of the portal source after the cycle (own check, 2026-11-25) adds one path. The portal pays a refund only inside processWithdrawals, which the zone's sequencer sends (ZonePortal.sol 1386-1408, 1506-1529), and claimRefund pays only its own caller (1531-1539). The same processWithdrawals call also delivers callback withdrawals: any zone account can request one (zone outbox request_withdrawal, outbox/mod.rs 159-262), and when the zone's gateway mode is open the messenger calls onWithdrawalReceived on any target (ZoneMessenger.sol 37-82). sync needs no unlock (PoolManager.sol:279) and the synced currency and reserves live in transient storage until the end of the transaction. So an account that has one callback withdrawal before the refund and one after it in the same batch can call sync(token) in the first callback and unlock, settle and take in the second. settle then counts the refund as that account's payment (PoolManager.sol:358-364).
findings.impact: No funds of liquidity providers or claim holders move. The party that named the deposit address, or the router or user it acted for, loses the refund of a failed deposit. The refund stays in the portal's refund registry, stays in the PoolManager as surplus, or goes to an account that placed callback withdrawals around it in the same portal batch. The loss to the taker is the same in all three cases.
findings.preconditions: T15 active on mainnet with TIP-1094 in its scope (the T15 page lists only TIP-1166 so far; the code gates TIP-1094 on T15). A zone with a nonzero id below next_zone_id and a key version other than 0. For the capture path: the zone's gateway mode is open, the taker's deposit fails in the zone, and the other account's two callback withdrawals sit on either side of the refund in one processWithdrawals transaction. The zone orders its withdrawal queue, so the account cannot force that position; it can only keep callback withdrawals flowing.
findings.mitigations: Routers and front ends should refuse take recipients whose bytes 4 to 12 are 0xFC on Tempo, or pay zone deposits from their own address so refunds return to them. Nothing in the PoolManager can be changed to stop the capture, because sync is open by design.

verification.factCheck: Fetched tempo/v1.19.1 crates/precompiles/src/tip20/mod.rs. transfer (lines 869-884) calls validate_transfer, which calls Recipient::resolve_transfer (line 1253); from T15 resolve_transfer (lines 1679-1695) decodes a zone deposit address, rejects version 0 and zone ids of 0 or at least next_zone_id, and sets the target to portal_address(zone_id). _transfer credits the portal (line 877) and deposit_virtual (lines 1073-1115) then calls depositVirtual with originator equal to the token's msg_sender, refuses zero amounts, caps grossAmount at u128 and turns any portal revert into a revert of the whole transfer. address_registry.rs lines 29-30 and 51-52 define the format as 0xFC in bytes 4 to 12. tips.sh/1094 says a failed deposit refunds the originator on Tempo after the batch settles, minus the processing fee, that there is no refund address field, and that a parked refund needs the refund recipient to act. upgrades.md lists T15 mainnet as 15 December 2026 (target) and t15.md says it covers only TIP-1166 so far and the scope may change. web3_clientVersion at https://rpc.mainnet.tempo.xyz returned tempo/v1.19.1-a9d6748/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu on this run, so the T15-gated code is in the running client but T15 is not active.
verification.codeCheck: take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297) charges the caller -amount.toInt128() and then calls currency.transfer(to, amount) (src/types/Currency.sol:56-80), which requires success and a return of 1 or empty. The TIP-20 debit equals amount, so the PoolManager loses exactly what the caller owes, and the unlock delta check forces the caller to settle it. A refund paid later to the PoolManager arrives in a separate transaction, so transient reserves set by sync (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288) do not cover it and _settle (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364) credits only reservesNow - reservesBefore inside one transaction. The refund therefore becomes surplus no ordinary caller can claim. The PoolManager has no generic call path, so a parked refund registered to it cannot be claimed. I found no path where the forwarding changes the amount debited or moves another user's balance.
verification.corrections: severity: low rather than info. The difference does create an integration hazard, because a user or router that names a zone deposit address as take recipient loses the refund of a failed deposit. It is not info under SCHEMA.md since a loss path exists, but the loss falls only on the party that chose the recipient, so it does not reach liquidity providers or claim holders. The actor value unprivileged is correct for triggering it; the victims are the actor or its own users, not uninvolved users.

findings.title: A bridge payment addressed to the PoolManager, delivered by a relay that any account may execute, can be run between that account's own sync and settle and booked as its payment
findings.difference: Circle's CCTP v2 contracts are deployed at TokenMessengerV2 0x28b5a0e9C621a5BadaA536219b3a228C8168cf5d and MessageTransmitterV2 0x81D40F21F12A8F0E3252Bccb954D722d4c464B64 on 13 of the 21 networks. receiveMessage mints USDC to the mintRecipient named on the source chain inside whatever transaction calls it, and when the message's destinationCaller is zero any account may call it. On Arc the mint is native USDC, which the PoolManager also sees through the ERC-20 face at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000. The same shape exists for canonical bridges. Several canonical bridges let any account run the last step of someone else's transfer in its own transaction. OP Stack L2CrossDomainMessenger.relayMessage replays a failed message for any caller (live messenger code on OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and MegaETH; on X Layer its nonce is still 0). On Ethereum, OptimismPortal2.finalizeWithdrawalTransactionExternalProof finalizes any proven withdrawal for any caller, Arbitrum's Outbox.executeTransaction executes any proven L2 to L1 message, and the LxLy bridge claimAsset pays any proven deposit. X Layer runs the same LxLy bridge (networkID 3). Polygon's StateReceiver at 0x1001 replays failed state syncs for any caller. Avalanche's TeleporterMessenger accepts delivery from any relayer when the message's allowedRelayerAddresses list is empty. Each of these ends in a plain ERC-20 transfer or mint to the recipient named by the original sender.
findings.mechanism: The base case is CCTP. Someone burns USDC on another chain with mintRecipient equal to this network's PoolManager and destinationCaller zero, and Circle attests the message. Any account calls unlock (src/PoolManager.sol:104-114). In the callback it calls sync(USDC) (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), which records balanceOf(PoolManager). It then calls MessageTransmitterV2.receiveMessage(message, attestation); the destination caller check passes because the field is zero (MessageTransmitterV2.sol lines 300-305), the nonce is marked used (line 221), and TokenMessengerV2._handleReceiveMessage mints amount minus fee to the PoolManager (TokenMessengerV2.sol lines 405-422, BaseTokenMessenger.sol lines 330-355). The callback then calls settle; _settle credits the difference (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364) to the caller, which takes it out with take (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297). On Arc the same sequence uses sync(0x3600...) and the face credit. CCTP v1 receiveMessage has the same destinationCaller rule (MessageTransmitter.sol lines 269-274). CCTP v2 hookData is only carried in the message; TokenMessengerV2 never executes it, so the mint recipient's own code does not run. The canonical bridge paths work the same way. The executor calls unlock, calls sync(token) in the callback (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), then calls the relay function with the public proof or message: relayMessage of a failed message whose target is the L2 standard bridge (CrossDomainMessenger.sol lines 239-248, StandardBridge.sol lines 272-299 mints or transfers to _to with no call to it), finalizeWithdrawalTransactionExternalProof (OptimismPortal2.sol lines 701-730, which takes the prover as an argument), Outbox.executeTransaction (AbsOutbox.sol lines 158-174) reaching L1ArbitrumGateway.finalizeInboundTransfer and safeTransfer to _to (L1ArbitrumGateway.sol lines 104-125, 139-146), claimAsset (PolygonZkEVMBridgeV2.sol line 453 onward, no caller restriction), replayFailedStateSync or replayFailedStateSyncWithData (StateReceiver.sol lines 85-103) reaching the PoS ChildChainManager deposit, or receiveCrossChainMessage (TeleporterMessenger.sol lines 242 and 284, _checkIsAllowedRelayer lines 596-613) reaching an ICTT token home or remote. When the recipient is the PoolManager its token balance rises inside the callback, and settle credits the rise to the executor (src/PoolManager.sol:358-364), who takes it. Relay paths by network: CCTP receiveMessage with destinationCaller zero on Ethereum, OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, World Chain, Ink, X Layer, Arbitrum One, Polygon, Avalanche, Monad, HyperEVM and Arc; replay of a failed L2CrossDomainMessenger message on OP Mainnet, Base, Unichain, Zora, World Chain, Ink, Soneium, Celo and MegaETH; OptimismPortal2 external-proof finalisation, Arbitrum Outbox execution and LxLy claimAsset on Ethereum; LxLy claimAsset on X Layer; StateReceiver replay on Polygon; Teleporter delivery with an empty relayer list on Avalanche. F-135 is the Tempo member of this class (zone portal refunds from the T15 fork).
findings.impact: The executor takes the bridged amount. The money belongs to whoever bridged it and named the PoolManager as recipient. No liquidity provider or claim holder funds move. A transfer of this kind that completes in a plain transaction (Circle's relayer, the first OP deposit relay, an auto-relayed Teleporter message, a claim sent by a bridge service) leaves the tokens in the PoolManager as surplus that no caller can claim, so in that case the bracket only takes money its owner had already lost, as in F-135. The loss is new only when the owner's integration planned to run the relay inside its own unlock (sync, relay, settleFor the user) and an outsider runs it first; the owner's later relay then reverts on the used nonce or spent message.
findings.preconditions: A CCTP burn on another chain with mintRecipient equal to the PoolManager of the destination network and destinationCaller zero, and its attestation, which Circle publishes through its public attestation API. The attacker needs no role and only has to send its transaction before the intended relayer. No such mint was found on Ethereum, Unichain, Ink or World Chain (see leadResults for L-772); other networks were not enumerated. For the canonical bridges: A bridge transfer whose final recipient is the PoolManager of the destination network and whose last step is still pending: a failed OP messenger message, an unfinalized OP or Arbitrum withdrawal or unclaimed LxLy deposit to the Ethereum PoolManager, a pending failed Polygon state sync carrying a PoS deposit to the Polygon PoolManager, or a Teleporter message with no relayer restriction. No such pending item was found: the one decoded pending Polygon PoS deposit (state id 3213072) pays 0x08bb17cf80ed16483efa0217480c94c233dd9900. Other bridges were not enumerated.
findings.mitigations: Integrations that bridge into a PoolManager should set the CCTP destinationCaller to their own receiver contract, restrict the Teleporter relayer list, or receive the funds in their own contract and pay the PoolManager inside their own sync and settle. Front ends and routers should never accept the PoolManager as a bridge recipient. Nothing in the PoolManager can change this, because sync is open by design.

findings.title: Source disagrees with two interface comments and two test conditions, and none of the four changes who can move funds
findings.difference: None. These are differences inside the repository, between src and its own comments and tests.
findings.mechanism: First, src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 says collectProtocolFees reverts if the contract is unlocked. The code checks only the caller and whether the currency is the synced ERC-20 (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52). _isUnlocked is declared at ProtocolFees.sol:60 and implemented at src/PoolManager.sol:391-394 and nothing calls it. The tests agree with the code: they expect ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced in both lock states (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1039). Second, src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:111 says only initialize and updateDynamicLPFee can be called without unlocking. sync has no onlyWhenUnlocked modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279) and test/Sync.t.sol:36-41 calls it while locked. Third, test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:129 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut when amountSpecified >= 0 at a 100 percent fee, while src/libraries/Pool.sol:311-316 reverts only for amountSpecified > 0 and line 320 returns a zero delta for amountSpecified == 0. Fourth, Pool.t.sol:143 treats a zeroForOne price limit below MIN_SQRT_PRICE as out of bounds, while Pool.sol:328 also rejects a limit equal to MIN_SQRT_PRICE. I traced each one for a fund effect. Fee collection inside an unlock changes protocolFeesAccrued and the balance by the same amount and touches no delta. A sync outside an unlock only sets two transient slots that the next sync overwrites. The zero amount swap changes no state. The stricter limit keeps slot0.tick from reaching MIN_TICK - 1.
findings.impact: No loss or freeze found. A reader who trusts the two interface comments gets the wrong picture of when sync and fee collection can run. The fuzz test at Pool.t.sol:129 would fail on an input with amountSpecified equal to zero and a 100 percent fee if the fuzzer produces one.
findings.preconditions: None for the mismatch itself. I could not run forge in this environment, so I do not know whether the current fuzz seed reaches the failing input.
findings.mitigations: The deployer can correct the two comments, decide whether collectProtocolFees should use _isUnlocked or drop it, and align the two test conditions with the source.

verification.factCheck: On chain I called sync(address(0)) from an unrelated address, with no unlock, on all 21 PoolManagers, and every call returned success. take from the same address reverted with ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d) on all 21. collectProtocolFees from that address reverted with InvalidCaller (0x48f5c3ed) on all 21. With the stored fee controller as sender and the manager locked it returned an amount on the eight networks that have a nonzero controller. These calls show that the deployed contracts accept sync while locked, which is what the code does and what the comment at src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:111 denies. They do not show what collectProtocolFees does while unlocked, since a read only call cannot open an unlock with the controller as caller. That part rests on the source and the tests. Inside the repository the four mismatches are as the finding states, with the one correction below.
verification.codeCheck: src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 says collectProtocolFees reverts if the contract is unlocked. src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52 checks only the caller and the synced ERC-20. _isUnlocked is declared at src/ProtocolFees.sol:60, implemented at src/PoolManager.sol:391-394 and in two test contracts, and nothing calls it. test/PoolManager.t.sol:1010-1039 attempts collection inside an unlock and expects ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced, so the tests agree with the code. src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:111 names initialize and updateDynamicLPFee as the only functions callable without unlocking, while sync has no modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279) and test/Sync.t.sol:36-41 calls it directly. test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:129 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut for amountSpecified >= 0, while src/libraries/Pool.sol:311-316 reverts only for a positive amount and line 320 returns a zero delta. test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:143 compares with < MIN_SQRT_PRICE and src/libraries/Pool.sol:328 with <=. I traced each for a fund effect. Collection lowers protocolFeesAccrued and the balance by the same amount (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56), touches no delta and cannot run between sync and settle of the same ERC-20 in either lock state. Fees accrued by a swap that is not yet paid can be collected inside the same unlock, and the unlock reverts as a whole unless the swapper settles (src/PoolManager.sol:112). PoolManager.swap rejects a zero amount (src/PoolManager.sol:193), so Pool.swap sees zero only when a beforeSwap hook delta cancels the amount (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:273-279), and then it changes no state. The stricter price limit stops a swap from ending at MIN_SQRT_PRICE and blocks no withdrawal.
verification.corrections: The fourth item cannot make the test fail. When the limit equals MIN_SQRT_PRICE the test takes neither branch and makes no swap call (test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:135-146), and test/utils/Deployers.sol:43 defines MIN_PRICE_LIMIT as MIN_SQRT_PRICE + 1, which matches the source. The third item is a failing input for the fuzz test whenever the fuzzer picks an LP fee of 1,000,000 together with amountSpecified 0. The setter setIsUnlocked in src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol:27-29 is also unused by any test, which is a further sign that a lock check on fee collection was planned or removed. ASSUMPTIONS.md A12 words the guard as unlocked and synced. The code applies it whenever the ERC-20 is synced, in both lock states.

findings.title: sync runs while the manager is locked and fee collection ignores the lock, and the mainnet fee controller lets anyone trigger collection
findings.difference: On mainnet the protocol fee controller is a V4FeeAdapter contract whose collect and triggerFeeUpdate functions have no access check. Any account can therefore make the PoolManager execute collectProtocolFees and setProtocolFee at a moment it chooses, including inside its own unlock callback. Mainnet also lets several users' operations share one transaction through ERC-4337 bundles and EIP-7702 batches.
findings.mechanism: sync has no onlyWhenUnlocked modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), so anyone can set the synced currency and reserves at any point of a transaction, and the value stays until a settle or another sync in that transaction. collectProtocolFees checks the caller and then reverts only if the currency is an ERC-20 equal to the synced currency (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52). It never calls _isUnlocked, which is declared at src/ProtocolFees.sol:60 and implemented at src/PoolManager.sol:391-394 with no caller. ASSUMPTIONS.md A12 describes the guard as depending on the unlocked state; the code does not. I walked the fund-moving paths for a gain and found none. Collection of the synced ERC-20 is blocked regardless of lock state, so the balance cannot fall between a sync and its settle through this path. Native settlement uses msg.value and no balance (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). Collection is bounded by protocolFeesAccrued with checked subtraction (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-55) and the adapter fixes the recipient. A sync left behind by an earlier operation in a bundle is overwritten by the next sync and cleared by the next ERC-20 settle (src/PoolManager.sol:361). What remains is that a stale sync makes a later native settle with value revert with NonzeroNativeValue if its caller did not sync first (src/PoolManager.sol:356), and makes collection of that currency revert for the rest of the transaction.
findings.impact: No loss or lasting freeze found. Within one transaction, a party that runs earlier can make a later native settle or a fee collection revert.
findings.preconditions: For the revert cases the two parties must share a transaction, for example an ERC-4337 bundle, and the later party must settle native currency without calling sync first. This is my own reading of the code and has not been checked by a second reviewer.
findings.mitigations: Integrators should call sync immediately before every settle, including native, as the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 says. The deployer can decide whether sync should require the unlocked state and whether collectProtocolFees should check it, and can correct the A12 text either way.

verification.factCheck: The Sourcify record for 0x89a5d5bf00a27d55c02951e49078a5c5771051db is an exact match named V4FeeAdapter. In src/feeAdapters/V4FeeAdapter.sol, triggerFeeUpdate at lines 72 to 74 and collect at lines 87 to 94 have no access modifier. collect calls POOL_MANAGER.collectProtocolFees(TOKEN_JAR, p.currency, p.amount), and the fee value passed to setProtocolFee comes from the pool override or the policy at lines 61 to 67 and 133 to 143. On chain at block 26470974 PoolManager.protocolFeeController() returned that adapter, the adapter's POOL_MANAGER() returned the PoolManager, TOKEN_JAR() returned 0xf38521f130fccf29db1961597bc5d2b60f995f85, owner() and feeSetter() returned the timelock and policy() returned 0x1cd822b70a0591420f65e94b9b3a0d0b0fb3a314. The TokenJar source has an empty receive function and a release function limited to the releaser, which is 0x0d5cd355e2abeb8fb1552f56c965b867346d6721 on chain. ERC-4337 says transient storage persists across UserOperations in one bundle and must be cleaned up manually when it guards access. I read only the adapter and jar files in the Sourcify bundles.
verification.codeCheck: sync has no modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), and the repository's tests call it while locked (test/Sync.t.sol:36-41, test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1023). collectProtocolFees checks the caller and then reverts when the currency is an ERC-20 equal to the synced currency (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52). It does not read the lock. _isUnlocked is declared at src/ProtocolFees.sol:60 and implemented at src/PoolManager.sol:391-394, and a search of src finds no caller. The comment at src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 says the call reverts if the contract is unlocked. The code and the tests at test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1038 behave otherwise. I traced the fund paths myself. The synced check does not depend on the lock, so collection of a synced ERC-20 always reverts and the balance cannot fall between a sync and its settle through this call. Collection of another currency during an unlock lowers the balance by at most protocolFeesAccrued (checked subtraction at src/ProtocolFees.sol:55) and changes no delta. Fees accrue in _swap before the swapper pays (src/PoolManager.sol:238), and the swapper's negative delta must be cleared before unlock returns (src/PoolManager.sol:112) or the whole transaction reverts, collection included. Native settlement credits msg.value only (src/PoolManager.sol:353-354). A collection with the PoolManager as recipient leaves an ERC-20 balance unchanged and reverts for native currency, because src has no receive or fallback function. A sync left by an earlier caller gives a later settler credit only for a real balance increase since that sync, and a native payment then reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:356), which test/PoolManager.t.sol:987-988 covers. I found no path that raises a settle credit or pays out more than accrued fees. This agrees with the researcher and answers the researcher's first lead from a second reading.
verification.corrections: The code facts hold on every network. Only the permissionless controller is specific to mainnet. The repository's own tests expect the present behaviour, so the disagreement is between the code and two texts: the comment at src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40 and assumption A12. The synced check as written rejects collection in more situations than a check tied to the lock would, so the difference removes no protection.

findings.title: Four interface comments and two test helper remarks disagree with the source, and none of them changes who can move funds
findings.difference: None. These are differences between the source text and the repository's own comments, tests and test doubles. They are the same on every network.
findings.mechanism: This unit compared every NatSpec sentence in src/interfaces with the function it describes and read every helper in src/test and test/utils. Six statements do not match the source, in addition to the four recorded in F-006. First, src/interfaces/IHooks.sol:102 says the fee returned by beforeSwap is used only if it is at most 1,000,000. The source reverts with LPFeeTooLarge when the override flag is set and the fee is above the maximum (src/libraries/Pool.sol:303-305, src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:75-78). The test agrees with the source and expects the revert (test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol:151-162), although its own comment says the large fee is not used. Second, IHooks.sol:50 and IHooks.sol:81 describe the delta handed to afterAddLiquidity and afterRemoveLiquidity as the sum of principal, fees and hook delta. The source passes principal plus fees, and subtracts the hook delta only after the hook returns (src/PoolManager.sol:171-178, src/libraries/Hooks.sol:219-243). The test doubles rely on the source behaviour (src/test/FeeTakingHook.sol:54-91, test/CustomAccounting.t.sol:270-322). Third, src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:85-86 calls the Swap event amounts the deltas of the pool's balances. The emitted values are the swapper's deltas, negative for the amount paid in (src/PoolManager.sol:241-250), and the tests expect -100 and 98 for an exact input of 100 (test/PoolManager.t.sol:500-503). Fourth, IPoolManager.sol:174 says take reverts if the requested amount is not available. That holds for native currency and for tokens with code, and test/PoolManager.t.sol:917-922 states it for an empty manager. For a currency address without code the transfer call succeeds with empty return data and nothing moves (src/types/Currency.sol:60-74), which earlier cycles recorded under assumption A4. Fifth, test/utils/CurrencySettler.sol:20-25 settles native currency without a prior sync and says a sync is not required, while the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 tells integrators to call sync before a native settle. A native settle that follows a token sync by other code in the same transaction reverts with NonzeroNativeValue (src/PoolManager.sol:353-356, test/PoolManager.t.sol:976-989). Sixth, src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol:27-33 offers setIsUnlocked and an _isUnlocked override, no test calls setIsUnlocked, and collectProtocolFees never reads the lock (src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57). This is the test double side of the first item of F-006. I traced each item for a fund effect. A hook that returns an oversized fee can only stop swaps in its own pool. The delta seen by a liquidity hook is the amount the hook can charge against, and the caller delta plus the hook delta still equals the pool delta in every replayed case. The event wording affects readers of logs only. The native settle revert needs code that runs earlier in the same transaction, and it returns the caller's value with the revert.
findings.impact: No loss or freeze found. A hook author who trusts IHooks.sol:102 may ship a hook that makes swaps in its own pool revert when it computes a fee above 100 percent. An integrator that copies the native branch of the test helper without sync(address(0)) can have a native settle reverted by a token sync left earlier in the same transaction.
findings.preconditions: None for the comments. The native settle revert needs a call to sync with a token address earlier in the same transaction, for example from a hook of a pool the caller used or from a contract that bundles several actions.
findings.mitigations: Correct the six texts. Hook authors should cap the fee before setting the override flag. Integrators should call sync(address(0)) before every native settle, as the comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 says.

verification.factCheck: The finding states no chain fact. Its field difference says that the six items are the same on every network, so the fact check is whether the deployed contracts behave as the source reading says. I ran read-only calls on all 21 RPC endpoints of state/networks.json on 2026-11-23 (Ethereum block 26,474,254, Celo 83,493,046, Polygon 97,792,226, Arc 32,649,308, the others at latest). From an unrelated address, sync(address(0)) returned success on all 21, sync of an address without code (0x00000000000000000000000000000000dead0001) reverted with empty data on all 21, settle() and take reverted with ManagerLocked (0x54e3ca0d) on all 21, and a call with empty calldata reverted on all 21. That matches the source: sync has no lock check, balanceOf on an address without code fails in the return decoding, and the contract has no receive or fallback function. For the fifth item I tested the guard on the deployed code. A caller placed by state override opened unlock, called sync(X) and then settle with 1 wei. Every path of that caller ends in a revert, so nothing is credited. With X set to the identity precompile 0x04, which answers balanceOf with its 36 input bytes, all 21 deployed PoolManagers returned NonzeroNativeValue (0xb0ec849e). The same caller with value 0 after sync(X), and with 1 wei after sync(address(0)), got past settle on all 21. With X set to the native face on Celo (0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438), Polygon (0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010) and Arc (0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000), and to USDC on Ethereum, the result was the same. The four interface comments and the two helper remarks are facts of this repository and I read each cited line. Not confirmed: forge is not installed, so I did not run the tests, and I did not exercise take with a currency without code inside an unlock on chain.
verification.codeCheck: All six items hold as stated. One. src/interfaces/IHooks.sol:102 says the returned fee is used only if it is at most 1,000,000. src/libraries/Pool.sol:303-305 calls removeOverrideFlagAndValidate when the override flag is set, and src/libraries/LPFeeLibrary.sol:75-78 with 43-45 reverts with LPFeeTooLarge above the maximum. test/DynamicReturnFees.t.sol:151-162 expects that revert, and its comment at line 158 says the large fee is not used. The comment at src/libraries/Hooks.sol:261-262 agrees with the source. Two. IHooks.sol:50 and 81 describe the delta passed to the hook as including the hook delta. src/libraries/Hooks.sol:219-243 encodes the delta it received, which src/PoolManager.sol:171 builds as principal plus fees, and subtracts the hook delta only at lines 230 and 242. src/test/FeeTakingHook.sol:53-91 computes its fee from that value. Three. src/interfaces/IPoolManager.sol:85-86 calls the event amounts the deltas of the pool balance. src/PoolManager.sol:241-250 emits the delta that src/libraries/Pool.sol:451-462 builds, which is negative for the amount paid in, and test/PoolManager.t.sol:500-503 expects -100 and 98. Four. IPoolManager.sol:174 says take reverts if the amount is not available. src/types/Currency.sol:60-74 accepts a call that does not revert and returns no data, with no code size check, so take of a currency without code debits the caller and moves nothing. Five. test/utils/CurrencySettler.sol:20-25 settles native currency without sync and says sync is not required. The comment at src/PoolManager.sol:348 asks for sync first. Lines 353-356 revert with NonzeroNativeValue when a token is synced and value is sent, and test/PoolManager.t.sol:976-989 covers it. Six. src/test/ProtocolFeesImplementation.sol:27-33 has setIsUnlocked and an _isUnlocked override. A search of test/ and src/ finds no call to either, and src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57 never reads the lock. I traced each item for a path to funds and looked for missed guards. An oversized override fee reverts the swap before any state change in Pool.swap, so it can only stop swaps in the pool of that hook. The delta shown to a liquidity hook does not change the sum: Hooks.sol:230 and 242 subtract the hook delta from the caller delta, and PoolManager.sol:181-183 books both, so caller delta plus hook delta equals principal plus fees. The subtraction goes through the int128 casts of src/types/BalanceDelta.sol:34-46. The event wording touches no accounting. A take of a currency without code leaves the caller with a negative delta in that id (PoolManager.sol:294). sync of the same address reverts, mint adds to the debt (line 326), clear accepts only a positive delta (lines 311-314), and a pool can return that currency only after someone paid it in, so the unlock ends in CurrencyNotSettled (line 112). The native settle revert returns the value to the caller. Fee collection is limited to the controller (ProtocolFees.sol:48) and to protocolFeesAccrued with a checked subtraction (line 55).
verification.corrections: No correction to the six items. Two precisions. The fourth item says the comment holds for tokens with code. It holds only for tokens whose transfer reverts or returns false on a shortfall, because Currency.sol:68 also accepts empty return data from a contract with code. The actor value is nominal here. The record describes no loss or freeze. The two operational effects need a hook author for the fee revert and a party that runs earlier in the same transaction for the native settle revert, which F-014 already records.

findings.title: Two more places where the repository's tests and test doubles disagree with the library source, and neither changes who can move funds
findings.difference: None. The disagreements are between files of this repository and hold on every network.
findings.mechanism: This extends F-006 with what a replay of test/libraries, test/Tick.t.sol, test/types and the test doubles in src/test found. First, test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:73-83 expects SafeCastOverflow from Pool.modifyLiquidity only when a token amount is above 2^128 - 1. The variable is named maxInt128InTypeU256 and holds Constants.MAX_UINT128. The source casts both amounts to int128: Pool.sol:212-235 takes the signed results of SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288 and SafeCast.toInt128 (SafeCast.sol:40-43) reverts once the amount of an add is above 2^127. For amounts from 2^127 + 1 to 2^128 - 1 the source reverts and the test expects success. One case from the replay: spacing 32767, price 735853766953812733719635225319847024411115828962 (tick 873548), range -131068 to 98301, liquidity 2300850342447660200206975412810193765, which is below the per tick cap 6076470837873901133274546561281575204. The amount of currency1 is 313585663563401618519606321096647269736 and the source reverts with SafeCastOverflow. Out of 400,000 random parameter sets 346 fell in this window. Every other outcome, including the order of the eight revert conditions at Pool.t.sol:51-70, matched the source. Second, src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol:144-197 asserts that the signed helpers return a positive amount for positive liquidity and a non-positive amount for negative liquidity. The source returns minus the rounded up amount for positive liquidity and the rounded down amount for negative liquidity (SqrtPriceMath.sol:266-270 and 283-287). On 200,000 random inputs the assertion for positive liquidity fails 135,655 times and the one for negative liquidity 48,354 times as written, and every other invariant of that file holds. The forge tests use the sign of the source: a negative delta is owed by the caller (PoolManager.sol:183 and 368-378), and test/libraries/StateLibrary.t.sol:300-301 negates the delta of an add to get the amount paid. The echidna harness is not part of forge test, so nothing in the repository runs it. Third, a correction to the fourth item of F-006: test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:135-158 calls swap for a nonzero amount only when it expects a revert. It makes no call for a valid limit and no call when a zeroForOne limit equals MIN_SQRT_PRICE, so that file says nothing about the boundary that Pool.sol:328-330 rejects and contains no successful nonzero swap. The third item of F-006 was replayed: 8,795 of 120,000 random cases had a zero amount with a 100 percent swap fee, where Pool.t.sol:129-131 expects InvalidFeeForExactOut and Pool.sol:311-320 returns a zero delta without touching state.
findings.impact: None on funds. In the first case the source refuses an add that the test would let through, so it is stricter than the test. A removal whose amount is 2^127 or more reverts at the same cast and has to be split, which an earlier cleared item on the int128 casts already covers. In the second case the source sign is the one the accounting in PoolManager needs: with the sign of the echidna file an add would credit the caller.
findings.preconditions: None. No account gains anything from these disagreements.
findings.mitigations: Change the bound at test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:73 to the int128 maximum and bring the sign assertions in src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol in line with SqrtPriceMath, so that the tests and the harness can serve as a reference for the source.

I checked each one against the text and with a Python transcription of the libraries that I wrote myself with EVM word semantics. Case one reproduces exactly. With spacing 32767 the per tick cap is 6076470837873901133274546561281575204. The price 735853766953812733719635225319847024411115828962 lies in tick 873548. The ticks -131068 and 98301 are multiples of 32767. getAmount1Delta rounded up for liquidity 2300850342447660200206975412810193765 gives 313585663563401618519606321096647269736, which is above 2^127 and below 2^128, and the source path reverts with SafeCastOverflow. Case two reproduces in direction. verification.codeCheck: Pool.modifyLiquidity passes the signed results of SqrtPriceMath.getAmount0Delta and getAmount1Delta through SafeCast.toInt128 in all three branches (src/libraries/Pool.sol:209-236). The signed helpers return minus the rounded up amount for a liquidity delta of zero or more and the rounded down amount for a negative delta (src/libraries/SqrtPriceMath.sol:261-288). toInt128(int256) reverts when the value does not fit (src/libraries/SafeCast.sol:40-43). An add therefore reverts when its rounded up amount is 2^127 + 1 or more, and a removal reverts when its rounded down amount is 2^127 or more. test/libraries/Pool.t.sol:73-83 compares the amounts with Constants.MAX_UINT128, so the source is the stricter side for amounts from 2^127 + 1 to 2^128 - 1. The eight earlier branches at Pool.t.sol:51-70 follow the order in which the source reaches them: checkTicks (Pool.sol:94-98), the underflow in LiquidityMath.addDelta for a negative delta on an empty tick (Pool.sol:529, src/libraries/LiquidityMath.sol:10-19), the empty position check (src/libraries/Position.sol:84-87), the cap on the lower tick before the upper tick (Pool.sol:165-173), and flipTick for the lower tick before the upper tick (Pool.sol:175-180). The sign in the source is the one the accounting needs. A negative delta is added to the caller's slot (src/PoolManager.sol:183 and 368-384), settle adds what was paid (PoolManager.sol:364) and unlock reverts while any slot is nonzero (PoolManager.sol:112). src/test/SqrtPriceMathEchidnaTest.sol:144-197 asserts the opposite sign. Pool.swap reverts at a 100 percent fee only for a positive amount and returns a zero delta for a zero amount before any state is written (Pool.sol:311-320), while Pool.t.sol:129 expects a revert for zero. Pool.t.sol:135-158 calls swap for a nonzero amount only inside the branches that expect a revert. I looked for a guard or a path that would turn one of these disagreements into a fund effect and found none. A removal that hits the cast can be split, because both amounts scale with the liquidity delta. PoolManager.swap rejects a zero amount (PoolManager.sol:193), so Pool.swap sees zero only when a beforeSwap hook cancels the amount in its own pool (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:273-279), and then nothing is written.

No forge test runs the harness. On the limit for an add: an amount of exactly 2^127 passes, because the amount is negated before the cast and -2^127 fits int128. A removal passes up to 2^127 - 1.

findings.title: The two lock guards that Trail of Bits finding 3 records as its fix are absent from the source, and the synced currency check that stands in their place skips address(0), which shares its balance with an ERC-20 address on five networks
findings.difference: On Ethereum no ERC-20 address reports the PoolManager's native balance. On five of the 21 networks one does: LegacyERC20ETH at 0xDeadDeAddeAddEAddeadDEaDDEAdDeaDDeAD0000 on Optimism and Zora, 0x0000000000000000000000000000000000001010 on Polygon, the CELO token 0x471EcE3750Da237f93B8E339c536989b8978a438 on Celo and 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 on Arc, where the figure is the native balance divided by 10^12. I read balanceOf(PoolManager) and eth_getBalance at one block per network and they agree on these five and on no candidate address of the other 16. Optimism, Polygon and Arc also have a fee controller whose collect function any account can call. Celo and Zora have no fee controller today.
findings.mechanism: 1. The report (printed page 33) describes the hazard: a fee collection between sync and settle lowers the balance, so the settle that follows credits less or reverts. Its fix review (printed page 62) records the fix as two guards: sync can be called only while the manager is unlocked, and collectProtocolFees reverts with ContractUnlocked while the manager is unlocked. 2. The source has neither guard. sync carries no modifier (src/PoolManager.sol:279-288). collectProtocolFees checks the caller and then reverts only when the currency is nonzero and equals the synced currency (src/ProtocolFees.sol:48-52). _isUnlocked is declared at src/ProtocolFees.sol:60 and implemented at src/PoolManager.sol:392-394 and has no caller. The interface still says the function reverts if the contract is unlocked (src/interfaces/IProtocolFees.sol:40) and declares ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced and no ContractUnlocked error (line 17). The tests of the repository expect the source behaviour in both lock states (test/PoolManager.t.sol:1001-1039) and call sync while locked (test/Sync.t.sol:36-41). 3. The check that replaced the guards closes the report's case when the collected id is the synced id. It compares ids and exempts address(0) with the comment that native settle uses msg.value. That reasoning assumes the native balance has no second id (A3). 4. Where a native face exists and a controller can be triggered, the report's sequence runs again across two ids: sync(face), collection of native fees, settle. My walk on the deployed PoolManagers of Optimism (block 159,929,377), Polygon (97,834,382) and Arc (32,774,161), with a stub placed at the controller address by state override, gave the same three answers on each: collection of the face id reverted with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced, collection of address(0) succeeded inside the unlock while the face was synced and paid out the accrued native fees (0.0407 ETH, 714.3 POL and 53.28 USDC), and the settle that followed reverted with a Panic from the checked subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360. On the other five controller networks the same walk with a stub token that returns the native balance of its argument gave the same answers. 5. A separate eth_call of collect((address,uint256)[]) with one entry for address(0) from an arbitrary account succeeded on all eight controllers, and each controller names one fixed TOKEN_JAR. 6. I traced who pays. Collection lowers protocolFeesAccrued by a checked subtraction before the transfer (src/ProtocolFees.sol:54-56), writes no delta and no transient slot, and pays the recipient the controller names. The lower balance reduces the credit of the account that holds the face bracket in that same transaction, or reverts its settle. A payer that syncs, transfers and settles without calling other code in between cannot be interleaved. The caller of collect gains nothing. 7. Two further effects follow from the absent guards. Any code that runs earlier in a shared transaction can leave sync(X) and make a later collection of X revert (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49-51), which contradicts the report's invariant UNI-ACTION-6 as worded (collectProtocolFees must not revert on valid input). The same stale sync makes a later native settle with value revert, which the ledger holds as F-071.
findings.impact: No loss of pool funds and no lasting freeze found. The account that syncs a native face and lets a native fee collection run before its settle loses credit equal to the collected amount or has its transaction reverted. Fee collection of a currency can be made to revert by an earlier sync in the same transaction. The finding extends F-014 from Ethereum to the eight networks with a controller and ties it to the audit record.
findings.preconditions: A fee controller that any account can trigger (Ethereum, Optimism, Base, Arbitrum One, Robinhood Chain, Polygon, BNB Smart Chain and Arc today). For the two id case also an address that reports the native balance (Optimism, Polygon and Arc today, and Celo and Zora once the owner sets a controller there). The affected party must itself hold a sync of the face while the collection runs.
findings.mitigations: Restore the lock check that the interface comment describes, or make the synced check cover address(0) as well. Contracts that harvest fees and settle in one transaction should collect before they sync. Routers should call sync themselves before each payment, native payments included.
